properties.statement: FOUR DIFFERENT NUMBERS DESCRIBING WHAT READS AS ONE SET WERE ALL LIVE AND ALL CORRECT, AND NOTHING IN THE SURFACE SAYS WHICH QUESTION EACH ANSWERED. Reported 2026-08-08 by dragon Boss f96eccd3, who credits the find to their worker w-4d05e937 for refusing to inherit a number from the brief. The boss had quoted '53 capabilities claim built' from scan_nodes. The worker produced four, all live at the same moment: status in {realized, verified} = 53, a STATUS-FIELD question; capabilities_verified = 56, has ANY Verification attached; realization.realized = 37, has an ARTIFACT that REALIZES it; and the population of gap:0a77650b58242054 = 48, the gap's own set. FOUR DIFFERENT PREDICATES OVER THE SAME NODE TYPE, EVERY ONE LEGITIMATE, AND NEITHER graph_report NOR loop_status LABELS WHICH IS WHICH — so a fleet quotes one of them for weeks believing it is THE number. THIS IS FIELD EVIDENCE FOR AN ACCEPTED REQUIREMENT NOTHING SATISFIES: req:a-surface-states-its-own-scope ('an output says which question it answered, and what it could not see') is accepted and currently sits in gap:45e43cc49581b991 with no capability delivering it. The half usually argued is 'what it could not see'; this report is the OTHER half — WHICH QUESTION IT ANSWERED — and it is the half that produced the error here, because all four numbers were complete and none was ambiguous about coverage. FIX SHAPE, theirs: name the predicate inline next to each count (`capabilities_verified: 56 (have >=1 VERIFIES edge)`), and/or let a rollup return the SET behind it so a denominator is auditable without re-deriving it by hand. Their formulation is worth keeping verbatim: A COUNT WHOSE DEFINITION TRAVELS WITH IT CANNOT BE QUOTED AS A DIFFERENT COUNT.
